banner.title: Connect your AI agent
banner.desc: Claude, Cursor or any other agent can run timers, see your missions and draft partnerships — straight from your editor.

title: Connect an AI agent to your account
subtitle: The agent you already work with can run your partnerships without opening a browser.
whatBody: MCP is an open protocol that lets an AI agent connect to outside services. The 1lev1 MCP server gives your agent access to your missions, timers and partnerships — and only yours. The skill installed alongside it teaches the agent how the platform works: what a rikma is, why logged hours are ownership, and what it must never do on somebody else's behalf.
quickBody: The command opens 1lev1 in your browser, you approve the connection, and the key is written into every agent you have installed — together with the skill.
quickNote: Restart your agent afterwards so it picks up the new configuration.
connectorTitle: From your phone and browser — no terminal
connectorBody: The Claude app, claude.ai and Claude Code in the browser connect through a connector: you paste one address, approve it in the browser, and that is it. No key to copy, no config file to edit.
connector_step1: Open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
connector_step2: Give it a name — 1lev1, for example — and paste the server address below.
connector_step3: Press Connect. A 1lev1 page opens; log in and approve the connection.
connector_step4: Done. One connection covers chat on your computer, the app on your phone and Claude Code in the browser.
connectorNote: The connection mints an ordinary API key on your account. It shows up on the API keys page and is revoked from there, exactly like a key created from the terminal.
pluginBody: If you work in Claude Code you can install the skill from the marketplace, then connect your account with the command above.
pluginNote: The plugin brings the knowledge; the connect command brings the access. You need both.
ex1: What am I supposed to be working on today?
ex2: Start the timer on the logo mission.
ex3: I worked three hours on the design yesterday — log it.
ex4: How many hours have I accrued in this partnership?
ex5: Turn this repo into a partnership with the three of us.
ex6: What is waiting for my approval?
boundaryTitle: What the agent will not do for you
boundaryBody: 1lev1 runs on consent, so the agent never performs an act that touches another person. Instead it prepares the form and sends you to approve it on the site.
boundary1: It does not vote or sign a profit-split in your place.
boundary2: It does not accept offers or change another member's standing in a partnership.
boundary3: It cannot see any other user's data — the key is bound to your account alone.
boundary4: Creating missions and tasks for other people is off by default and needs an explicit grant.
agentsBody: The command detects what you actually have installed and writes only to that: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Roo Code, Continue, Antigravity and VS Code. It leaves alone any config file it cannot parse, and backs up every file before changing it.
othersBody: The server speaks standard MCP, so it is not Claude-only. What works today:
other_chatgpt_how: turn on Developer mode in settings, add a connector with the same server address, and approve it in the browser. Paid plans only.
other_geminiCli_how: the connect command above writes to them directly, like any other editor.
other_geminiEnterprise_how: an admin adds a custom MCP server under Connected apps. That form needs a manual client id and secret — write to us and we will issue them for your organisation's callback address.
other_codex_how: added by hand to ~/.codex/config.toml, with the key living in an environment variable rather than in the file.
other_anyMcp_name: n8n, Zapier or an agent you wrote yourself —
other_anyMcp_how: any MCP client that speaks Streamable HTTP with an Authorization header works against the same address.
othersNote: The consumer Gemini app still does not let you add an MCP server yourself — connections there open only through partnerships with Google.
manualBody: If your agent is not on the list you can add the server by hand. Get the key from the command above.
security1: The key is a password in every practical sense. Do not share it, and do not commit it to git.
security2: Approving again from the site replaces the previous key and revokes the old access.
security3: To disconnect completely, this command removes the server and the skill from every agent.
security4: That command only cleans up your local configs — the key itself stays valid. To invalidate it, run the connect command again and approve: it replaces the previous key.
